episodes.title: Where Does Our Economic System Come From?
episodes.description: Economics is a broad and complex field, and it’s been influenced by tons of important thinkers over thousands of years.

episodes.title: What is opportunity cost?
episodes.description: Explore how limited resources and competing wants shape the movement of goods, services, and money.

episodes.title: What is the Circular Flow model?
episodes.description: The circular flow model serves as a powerful tool to explain the overall functioning of the economy.

episodes.title: The Game of Supply and Demand
episodes.description: The balance of supply and demand is at the heart of how prices are determined.

episodes.title: What is Market Equilibrium?
episodes.description: Explore market equilibrium, where supply meets demand, and how shifts change prices and availability.

episodes.title: What is GDP?
episodes.description: Gross Domestic Product is one of the most common measurements for the health of a national economy.

episodes.title: Can the Real GDP Please Stand Up
episodes.description: Examine why changing prices and product characteristics complicate comparisons of GDP and economic growth.

episodes.title: How Does Real GDP Per Capita Affect You?
episodes.description: In this episode of Study Hall: Macroeconomics, we discuss the use and accuracy of Real GDP Per Capita as a measure of an economy’s health.

episodes.title: How far does $20 go today vs. the 80s
episodes.description: In this episode, we’ll take a look at the Consumer Price Index to find out more about the cost of living.

episodes.title: Is inflation really that bad?
episodes.description: Inflation refers to across-the-board changes in prices, and calculating how much prices change over time is a big part of macroeconomics.

episodes.title: Why people work
episodes.description: Explore labor supply, income and substitution effects, labor–leisure tradeoffs, and workforce participation.

episodes.title: Why can’t I get a job?
episodes.description: In this video, Study Hall explains labor demand, how it’s determined, and what effects it has on real wages.

episodes.title: What kind of unemployed are you?
episodes.description: Examine different forms of unemployment to understand what the headline unemployment rate leaves out.

episodes.title: Do higher wages mean more unemployment?
episodes.description: Examine factors that shift equilibrium wages and complicate simple models of the labor market.

episodes.title: How do interest rates affect you?
episodes.description: We discuss interest rates, the role of savings, and external factors that affect the loanable funds market and equilibrium interest rate.

episodes.title: What affects your interest rate?
episodes.description: Explore the loanable funds market and the factors that influence real interest rates.

episodes.title: What is government debt?
episodes.description: Explore how governments raise money when tax revenue does not cover planned spending.

episodes.title: What is the financial market?
episodes.description: Examine banks’ role in moving funds between savers and people who want to spend or invest.

episodes.title: What is money?
episodes.description: This episode of Study Hall: Macroeconomics explains how money is measured, and how it multiplies in the banking system.

episodes.title: What is the Federal Reserve?
episodes.description: Explore the Federal Reserve as a form of government intervention intended to support economic growth.

episodes.title: What is our economy’s potential?
episodes.description: In this episode of Study Hall: Macroeconomics, we explore potential GDP and all of the factors that go into making it grow.

episodes.title: My Wages vs. Your Prices: Short-Run Aggregate Supply
episodes.description: Examine how prices and inflation affect short-run aggregate supply.

episodes.title: Can You Predict a Recession?
episodes.description: Look for patterns in economic cycles and consider whether they can help predict future changes.

episodes.title: Does what we spend matter?
episodes.description: When you combine all the spending in the whole economy, you’re looking at aggregate demand.

episodes.title: Real & Potential GDP: Understanding Equilibrium
episodes.description: Combine aggregate supply and demand to examine how economic shocks affect prices, output, and employment.

episodes.title: Is Fiscal Policy Keeping Us Alive?
episodes.description: Examine how government policies are intended to influence aggregate demand over time.

episodes.title: Is Our Economy Really Self-Driving?
episodes.description: Explore how central banks intervene when markets’ self-regulating forces are not enough.

episodes.title: What are the Long-Run Effects of Monetary Policy?
episodes.description: Consider monetary policy’s lasting effects by examining how an expanding money supply influences inflation.

episodes.title: Is Public Healthcare Good for the Economy?
episodes.description: In this episode of Study Hall: Macroeconomics, Matt talks about the positive effects of long-run fiscal policy on the economy and society as a whole.

episodes.title: Where does the government get its money?
episodes.description: In this episode of Study Hall: Macroeconomics, you’ll hear all about the consequences of government financing.

episodes.title: Economic Parenting Styles: Keynesian vs Neoclassical
episodes.description: There are a lot of different viewpoints on how an economy should run and how the government should influence the market.
